Chief Executive Officer (CEO)

El Dorado County Chamber of Commerce

El Dorado County, California

Compensation: $75,000-$85,000 + Benefits + Performance Incentive Opportunity

The El Dorado County Chamber of Commerce seeks an energetic, visionary, and results-oriented Chief Executive Officer to lead one of the region's most respected business organizations.
Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the CEO serves as the organization's chief executive, chief fundraiser, public advocate, and principal spokesperson. This position offers a unique opportunity for an entrepreneurial leader who enjoys building relationships, generating revenue, advocating for business, and creating meaningful community impact.
Key Responsibilities

Lead the Chamber's strategic vision and operations.
Serve as the primary advocate for the business community.
Build strong relationships with business leaders, elected officials, community organizations, and regional partners.
Drive membership recruitment, engagement, and retention.
Lead fundraising, sponsorship development, and revenue-generation initiatives.
Secure corporate partnerships and community investments.
Manage staff, finances, programs, and organizational operations.
Support and collaborate with the Board of Directors to achieve strategic objectives.

Fundraising & Revenue Development

A major component of this position is revenue generation through:
Corporate sponsorships
Strategic partnerships
Membership growth
Event sponsorships
Community investment programs
Fundraising campaigns

Candidates should demonstrate success in fundraising, business development, sponsorship sales, relationship management, membership growth, or revenue generation.
Qualifications

Bachelor's degree preferred.
Executive leadership experience in business, chamber management, nonprofits, associations, economic development, sales, public affairs, or related fields.
Strong communication and public speaking abilities.
Proven relationship-building skills.
Experience managing budgets and organizational operations.
Demonstrated success growing revenue and developing partnerships.

Compensation & Benefits

Base salary: $75,000-$85,000, depending on qualifications and experience, plus benefits and performance-based incentive compensation.

The CEO will be eligible for additional compensation tied to:
Fundraising growth
Sponsorship development
Membership growth and retention
Revenue enhancement
Strategic partnership development
Achievement of Board-approved organizational goals

Exceptional performance may result in total compensation exceeding $100,000 annually.

Benefits include:
Health Insurance
Paid Vacation, Sick Leave, and Holidays
Retirement Contribution Opportunities
Professional Development
Chamber and Professional Association Memberships
Mileage and Business Expense Reimbursement
Flexible Work Environment

The Chamber seeks an entrepreneurial leader who recognizes that fundraising, sponsorship development, and membership growth are essential components of organizational success. The CEO will have substantial opportunities to increase total compensation through successful revenue generation, strategic partnerships, and achievement of organizational growth objectives.

Organizational Description

Alameda Health Consortium is the association of community health centers in Alameda County, California. The Consortium supports the involvement of communities in achieving comprehensive, accessible health care and improved outcomes for the underserved in the county. The Consortium’s policy, advocacy, and program activities have resulted in our becoming a credible, trusted leader in promoting and improving the quality of health care for our communities. Our vigorous pursuit of community alliances and our dedication to collaborative efforts help eliminate duplication of services and ensure that we continue to deliver affordable and coordinated services that honor both the health care needs and the cultures of those we serve.

The Community Health Center Network (CHCN), sister organization to the Alameda Health Consortium, is made up of the eight federally qualified community health centers in Alameda County.  CHCN functions as the managed care MSO for our health centers. To help our health centers meet their missions of providing the best possible care to their communities, we also provide a broad range of training, technical assistance, quality improvement, information technology, and data analytic services.

Position Title: Chief Executive Officer

Department: Administration

Reports To: Board of Directors

Classification: Exempt

Status: Full-Time Regular

Position Summary

The CEO works closely with Board of Directors to develop and advance the vision, mission and strategic plan for AHC and CHCN and has ultimate responsibility for the achievement of strategic initiative results . The CEO works collaboratively with the Internal E xecutive Team to direct strategic, operational and capacity building initiatives across the two agencies .

IDEAL CANDIDATE QUALITIES

The CEO of AHC/CHCN will be   able to lead t he two entities as part of one interconnected organization , with teams and initiatives   that cross each other seamlessly.
The ideal CEO will be able to gain the trust of all the Board members and honor the perspectives that   each brings to the table, whether they are longer-serving or newer members.
The CEO   will bring humility and integrity to the role and will be an effective communicator and consensus builder.
The public facing aspect of the CEO role requires someone who is assertive and strategic, and who is   able to  build lasting partnerships with external partners, while strongly advocating for the interests of the   populations we serve.
The CEO must be committed to the needs of the diverse populations we serve and understand   the particular challenges we face in light of the existing racial, cultural, and socioeconomic disparities.
The CEO will bring a palpable love and passion for the mission of the organization that will   be informed and evidenced by prior work and advocacy experiences.
The CEO will work closely with the Executive Team to manage the daily operations of both organizations. The Executive Team is made of highly   knowledgeable   and accomplished professionals who already work   together very well .

Essential Position Results

Leads AHC & CHCN to advocacy visions and strategic goals determined by the Board of Directors .
Collaborates with the Executive Team to create strategic operational plans with initiatives for each organization to develop, strengthen and ensure sustainability .
Maintains open communication with the Board of Directors, reporting any significant information and i nform ing the board of any changes in the organization’s current status and advising on the most preferred resolutions and strategies to meet the organizations’ goals and objectives .
Represents the organizations at external stakeholder meetings. Attends community events in an effort to build and maintain positive relationships with local community-based organizations.
Develops, maintains, and advance key external partnerships with elected officials, public agencies, health systems, Medi-Cal managed care plans, etc.
Advises leadership on contract negotiations with existing grant funders as well as federal, state and local funding opportunities for continued support of clinic programs.
Works closely with the Chief Impact Officer to o versee policy and regulatory changes that impact our organizations and efforts to advocate on behalf of our members.
Directs the Leadership Team to implement and operationalize the strategic plan with initiatives that strengthen the organization and ensure its sustainability.
Fosters and maintains open communication with the Board of Directors, reporting any significant issues, informing the Board of any changes in the organization’s current status , and advising on possible resolutions and strategies to meet the organization’s goals and objectives .
Works closely with the Eligibility and Enrollment Team to create and or implement programs in support of eligibility and enrollment.
Works closely with the Director of Development in the development of programs and services that provide value for our members and create revenue and funding streams to support our member health centers . Oversight of the administrative and performance monitoring of grants and contracts; including compliance, progress reports, training and evaluation.
Actively delegates operational work to the Executive Team and sets high standards and expectations for performance at the Chief level and throughout the organization.

Experience Qualifications

A minimum of 15 years of professional experience, with a minimum of 10 years senior leadership experience.

jobs.description:
About Berkeley

At the University of California, Berkeley, we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth. We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.

We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan, which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.

Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride.

Departmental Overview

University Development and Alumni Relations (UDAR) increases support for and enhances knowledge of UC Berkeley through communications, public outreach, and fundraising. The department is responsible for centralized fundraising and donor engagement and works to strengthen unit development offices by consulting and partnering with campus fundraisers. University Development and Alumni Relations also handles a range of central activities and services encompassing events, communications, stewardship, prospect development, gift management, database management, and more.

Position Summary

The Executive Director, Campaign Planning designs, develops, delivers, and administers the University’s comprehensive campaign and associated fundraising programs, working in consultation with campaign counsel and the Vice Chancellor of University Development and Alumni Relations and Associate Vice Chancellor Constituent Programs. This strategic position works closely with campus leadership and fundraising leaders and volunteers to support and deliver measurable annual and long-term outcomes. This position collaborates closely with partners on the development of campaign materials, marketing plans, and organizing related programs/events; it cultivates, stewards, and may solicit donor prospects. This position reports to the Associate Vice Chancellor, Constituent Programs, UDAR with a dotted line report to the Vice Chancellor, University Development and Alumni Relations.

Application Review Date

The First Review Date for this job is September 7, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before September 28, 2026. The job will be open until filled.

Responsibilities

Campaign planning and direction

Serves as an expert or lead development professional in campaign planning and direction, which has an environment that includes donors capable of making very significant contributions to the campus.
Develop, implement and assess progress of the campaign plan and recommend overall campaign strategies, including but not limited to campaign architecture (themes, overall goal, sub-goals); Timeline and phases; Volunteer organizational structure; Campaign team budget and staffing.
Collaborate with other UDAR units on campaign stewardship plan; Campaign communications plan; Campaign outreach and events plan.
Conduct and/or oversee the assessment of campaign feasibility and goal setting. Track and report on progress to goal at regular intervals throughout the campaign to high-level campus and volunteer leaders as well as UDAR management team.
Develop and track progress against the campaign timeline and recommend appropriate corrective action and/or campaign adjustments as appropriate.
Serve as primary liaison between UDAR and campaign counsel including scheduling consultation visits and phone calls, as well as receipting invoices and processing of payments.

Campus multidisciplinary themes

In collaboration with the Provost, Vice Chancellor for Research and deans, staff and manage the campus multidisciplinary themes during the public phase of the campaign, including development of transformational gift opportunities as well as identification, cultivation and solicitation of principal and major gift prospective donors.
Staff and manage the ongoing needs assessment and priority setting processes during the public phase of the campaign, including units, programs and other campus initiatives.

Marketing plans/strategies

Develops, creates, writes, implements, and/or evaluates individualized marketing plans and/or strategies for cultivation and solicitation of individual major gifts, gift planning, or corporate/foundation prospects (strategies typically require a high degree of innovation).
Attend meetings where strategies for principal gift-level prospects as well as prospects directly managed by the campaign director are discussed and help ensure that these strategies are developed in the context of the overall campaign strategy.

Executive advisor

Serves as an executive advisor for this area of expertise, interacting with prospects, donors, staff and outside professionals to provide information, advice and counsel regarding specialized program(s).
In partnership with AVC, Constituent Relations and AVC, Development, develop an internal communications strategy to keep colleagues within development/advancement and across the university apprised of campaign priorities, progress, and status.
Attend meetings of UDAR fundraising teams, including PGSI, Major Gifts, and SED, on a regular basis to facilitate coordination with prospects and campaign strategies.
Attend and participate as appropriate in key meetings related to the campaign, such as: Board of Trustees and select committee meetings, as appropriate.
Needs assessment and priority setting meetings.
Campaign volunteer leadership meetings, including unit based advisory groups. Meetings with key stakeholders to plan and implement multidisciplinary themes. Act as campaign liaison to other university offices as appropriate.
Convene specialized communities of practice to promote campaign goals and assessment

Prospect and volunteer constituencies

Creates, establishes and evaluates methods for building/maintaining prospect and volunteer constituencies and identifies, recruits, and directs the activities of high-level volunteers.
Working closely with the Vice Chancellor, provide staffing for the campaign chair/co-chairs and National Campaign Steering Committee, including: scheduling meetings; preparing agendas; briefing the Chancellor, Vice Chancellor, and campaign co-chairs; ensuring timely follow-up; and communicating committee decisions to relevant parties within development/advancement and across the university.
Develop individual relationships with NCSC co-chairs and members.
Oversee the development of campaign volunteer resources, such as handbooks, newsletters, and ongoing training opportunities to keep volunteers engaged with the campaign and its priorities, as well as high-level volunteer meetings and events, including the annual Volunteer Summit.

Fundraising and advancement programs / Fundraising goals

Analyzes needs and creates strategic and long-range plans for fundraising and other advancement programs and may have the authority to make commitments and precedent-setting decisions regarding program design, development, and procedures.
Working closely with appropriate colleagues in development/advancement services, including the AVC, Constituent Relations, AVC, PGSI, and AVC, Advancement, develop campaign gift tables, campaign counting and gift tagging protocols, campaign reports, and other tools required to track and report campaign progress, both for campus overall and individual units.
Ensures that predetermined fundraising goals are met.

Campaign team leadership

Manage and provide leadership for the campaign team. Establish and assess overall team strategy and goals. Mentor & coach team members.

Required Qualifications

Expert collaboration, relationship building, and trust building skills to work effectively with a broad range of stakeholders and partners.
Strong ability to navigate organizational complexities and decentralized environments and to lead successfully through influence.
Expert knowledge of comprehensive campaigns, particularly in a university setting.
Expert knowledge of various aspects of and functions in fundraising, such as donor and public relations, communications & marketing, planned giving, stewardship, and/or front-line fundraising, etc.
Expert knowledge of diverse stakeholder groups, teams, departments, achievements, and activities of a major and complex organization, including current issues of concern for both a research university campus and throughout higher education generally.
Expert knowledge of, and/or ability to quickly learn, the UC Berkeley campus including its vision, mission, goals, objectives, achievements and infrastructure; and/or demonstrated success in and expertise of (an) organization(s) with similarities to UC Berkeley.
Expert knowledge of all applicable laws, rules, regulations, risks, etc. in the nonprofit & fundraising field.
Expert written, oral, listening and interpersonal communication skills, including advanced political acumen, to establish and maintain good working relationships at all organizational levels and with outside constituencies, including donors and volunteers.
Expert skill in making persuasive and compelling presentations of campus goals/objectives and in securing gifts.
Expert analytical, critical thinking, problem solving, and conflict resolution skills.
Expert project/program management skills, including skill in setting and meeting program/project goals and objectives within budget and time constraints.
Demonstrated leadership experience, including the ability to build trust, influence others, and drive results.
Strong skills to lead and develop high-performing team(s), including setting strategic direction, establishing clear expectations, coaching staff, fostering collaboration, and managing accountability.

Education / Training

Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training. (Required)
Advanced degree (Preferred)

Salary & Benefits

For information on the comprehensive benefits package offered by the University, please visit the University of California's Compensation & Benefits website.

Under California law, the University of California, Berkeley is required to provide a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role and should not offer a salary outside of the range posted in this job announcement. This range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions, including but not limited to experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, analysis of internal equity, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be offered a salary at or near the top of the range for a position. Salary offers are determined based on final candidate qualifications and experience.

The budgeted annual salary range that the University reasonably expects to pay for this position is $175,400.00 - $240,000.00. The full range associated with the job classification is $142,400.00 - $279,400.00.

This is an exempt, monthly-paid position.
This is a full-time (40 hours/week) career position eligible for UC benefits.

How To Apply

To apply, please submit your resume and cover letter.

Other Information

This position will require a weekly on-site/on-campus presence with the possibility of some weekly telecommuting days, and it is not eligible for full remote work. Exact arrangements are determined in partnership with your supervisor to meet role responsibilities and department needs a

About BirchBark Foundation:
BirchBark Foundation is a nonprofit organization dedicated to protecting and honoring the human-animal bond. We act as a bridge between a crisis and a solution, providing financial assistance to vulnerable families faced with unaffordable medical expenses to save the life of a pet. We also support all families through education and pet loss counseling programs. We believe financial hardship should never cause the loss of a family pet. Our culture is collaborative, mission-driven, and rooted in compassion—for our clients, our veterinary partners, and each other.
Position Overview
BirchBark Foundation is seeking a strategic, compassionate, and growth-oriented Development Director
to lead our philanthropic operations. Reporting directly to the Executive Director, the Development Director will architect and execute a comprehensive fund development strategy designed to stabilize and grow BirchBark programs and fundraising.
This position is pivotal to building long-term financial sustainability and expanding our reach in Santa Cruz, Monterey, and San Benito counties. Working in close collaboration with the Executive Director and Board of Directors, this position will be responsible for the success of all fundraising campaigns, events, and outreach initiatives. This position will cultivate all efforts of the fund development plan, including major donor cultivation strategy, all fundraising events, overseeing grants, and community outreach efforts.

Key Responsibilities
Fundraising and Development
Create, execute, and sustain a multi-year term fund development plan designed to meet revenue goals and support BirchBark’s strategic growth.
Manage and grow a major gifts program, annual giving campaigns, planned giving, sponsorships, and oversee grants acquisition, pipeline and applications.
Identify and cultivate new and existing Corporate and Business partnerships. 
Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward donors and prospects while building strong relationships with donors, foundations, and community partners.
Prepare fundraising reports, revenue forecasts and donor stewardship plans
Work closely with leadership and staff to implement the fund development plan, including training and supporting staff and Board efforts. 
Support Development-related budgeting and revenue tracking.
Maintain consistent and accurate donor records and tracking through our CRM- Little Green Light.

Engagement and Communications 
Lead the vision, planning, sponsorship acquisition, and execution for BirchBark’s two major annual fundraising events
, ensuring high ROI and strong community alignment.
Find and run additional outreach events across our three-county service area to deepen local connections and expand organizational awareness.
Represent BirchBark at community events, speaking engagements and donor gatherings across Santa Cruz, Monterey, and San Benito counties. 

Grants Supervision & Institutional Giving
Oversee and support the foundation’s grant lifecycle, including pipeline research, strategy, proposal development, and timely impact reporting.
Ensure grant requests accurately reflect BirchBark's mission.

Cross-Functional Team Collaboration
Partner closely with the Marketing Manager
to ensure brand consistency, cohesive donor campaigns, and compelling direct-response fundraising messaging across digital and print channels.
Collaborate with the Help Line Supervisor
to transform PetAid success metrics and human-animal bond stories into impactful donor communications that reflect our core values.

Qualifications & Competencies
The ideal candidate is strongly aligned and passionate about our mission of preserving the human animal bond. 
5+ years of fund development experience, with demonstrated success in major donor cultivation, grant management, and event execution.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience.
Experience managing CRM’s (strong preference for LGL proficiency).
Ability to translate organizational goals into actionable fundraising plans and measurable targets.
Outstanding written and verbal communication skills; ability to articulate the profound value of saving the human-animal bond with professional warmth and accuracy.
Strong leadership style rooted in teamwork, working seamlessly alongside the Executive Director, program managers, and board members.
Familiarity with the philanthropic landscape of Monterey, Santa Cruz, and San Benito counties is strongly preferred.
Experience with Google Workspace, Slack and Asana.
Reliable transportation and the ability to represent BirchBark in Monterey, Santa Cruz and San Benito counties as needed.

Core Values Alignment
Every member of the BirchBark team embodies our four core values:
Compassion:
Leading with empathy for both pet guardians facing crisis and our veterinary partners.
Integrity:
Maintaining absolute stewardship of donor funds and transparency in aid distribution.
Collaboration:
Building safety nets through active teamwork and community partnership.
Positivity:
Bringing optimism, energy, and a solution-oriented spirit to our work every day.

License and Certifications
Certified Fund Raising Executive (CFRE) preferred; active within professional affiliations such as AFP, etc. preferred. 
Active driver’s license and insurance. 

Work Environment
This position may be hybrid or remote, with required availability for on-site presence during events and key planning meetings.
Local travel may be required throughout Santa Cruz, Monterey, and San Benito counties.
Evening and weekend work is expected during peak event seasons.

Physical Requirements & ADA Accommodations
This position regularly requires a combination of the following activities: speaking, hearing, standing, walking, sitting for extended periods, and occasionally lifting or carrying materials up to 25 pounds (e.g., event supplies). Participation in in-person meetings and community events is expected.
BirchBark Foundation is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you need accommodations during any part of the application or employment process, please contact us directly.

Benefits
Two weeks of accrued vacation + week between 12/24 and 1/1 
Insurance coverage: Health, Dental, Vision, Acupuncture, Chiropractic
10 Paid holidays with ability to take floating holiday 
Cell phone stipend
Mileage reimbursement 
Access to the CalSavers Retirement Savings Program

At ALSAC you do more than make a living; you make a difference.

We like people who are different…because we’re different, too. As one of the world’s most iconic and respected nonprofits, we know what it’s like to stand out. That’s why we’re looking at you. Your background, perspective, and desire to make an impact set you apart. As we work to help St. Jude cure childhood cancer, we're calling on the game-changers, innovators and visionaries to join our family. Not just for the kids of St. Jude, but also for you. Your leadership will be instrumental in not only meeting but surpassing revenue goals and fostering a culture of success within your team.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership: Drive significant growth in fundraising and fiscal KPIs, ensuring alignment with the budget for your assigned area.
Team Management: Lead and develop a team of dedicated people leaders and individual contributors, inspiring them to achieve excellence in fundraising events and campaigns.
Business Development: Expand a vital book of business, encompassing individual donors, corporations, and high-value volunteers, with a knack for securing six-figure gifts. Develop executive committees and/or boards to secure new fundraising opportunities.
Volunteer Engagement: Recruit, train, and collaborate with executive-level volunteers and committees, managing multiple active event volunteer committees.
Fundraising Innovation: Craft and implement strategies to enhance corporate and individual fundraising initiatives, with a focus on securing significant five and six-figure contributions.
Donor Relations: Manage donor leads effectively, working closely with the Prospect Development team to develop compelling donor proposals and maintain up-to-date contact information.
Staff Development: Oversee the day-to-day management and professional growth of your staff, including performance evaluations and staffing adjustments as necessary. This position will directly supervise individual contributors
Market Research: Stay abreast of market trends and developments within your territory to identify new business opportunities.
Performance Analysis: Conduct monthly reviews to pinpoint areas requiring attention and implement corrective actions.
Travel Requirements: Be prepared to travel throughout the area 25-30% of the year, including occasional weekends + 4-5 visits to Memphis.

Qualifications

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth. We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan, which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.

Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride.

Departmental Overview

University Development and Alumni Relations (UDAR) increases support for and enhances knowledge of UC Berkeley through communications, public outreach, and fundraising. The department is responsible for centralized fundraising and donor engagement and works to strengthen unit development offices by consulting and partnering with campus fundraisers. University Development and Alumni Relations also handles a range of central activities and services encompassing events, communications, stewardship, prospect development, gift management, database management, and more.

Position Summary

The Executive Director, Campaign Planning designs, develops, delivers, and administers the University’s comprehensive campaign and associated fundraising programs, working in consultation with campaign counsel and the Vice Chancellor of University Development and Alumni Relations and Associate Vice Chancellor Constituent Programs. This strategic position works closely with campus leadership and fundraising leaders and volunteers to support and deliver measurable annual and long-term outcomes. This position collaborates closely with partners on the development of campaign materials, marketing plans, and organizing related programs/events; it cultivates, stewards, and may solicit donor prospects. This position reports to the Associate Vice Chancellor, Constituent Programs, UDAR with a dotted line report to the Vice Chancellor, University Development and Alumni Relations.

Application Review Date

The First Review Date for this job is September 7, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before September 28, 2026. The job will be open until filled.

Responsibilities

Campaign planning and direction

Serves as an expert or lead development professional in campaign planning and direction, which has an environment that includes donors capable of making very significant contributions to the campus.
Develop, implement and assess progress of the campaign plan and recommend overall campaign strategies, including but not limited to campaign architecture (themes, overall goal, sub-goals); Timeline and phases; Volunteer organizational structure; Campaign team budget and staffing.
Collaborate with other UDAR units on campaign stewardship plan; Campaign communications plan; Campaign outreach and events plan.
Conduct and/or oversee the assessment of campaign feasibility and goal setting. Track and report on progress to goal at regular intervals throughout the campaign to high-level campus and volunteer leaders as well as UDAR management team.
Develop and track progress against the campaign timeline and recommend appropriate corrective action and/or campaign adjustments as appropriate.
Serve as primary liaison between UDAR and campaign counsel including scheduling consultation visits and phone calls, as well as receipting invoices and processing of payments.

Campus multidisciplinary themes

In collaboration with the Provost, Vice Chancellor for Research and deans, staff and manage the campus multidisciplinary themes during the public phase of the campaign, including development of transformational gift opportunities as well as identification, cultivation and solicitation of principal and major gift prospective donors.
Staff and manage the ongoing needs assessment and priority setting processes during the public phase of the campaign, including units, programs and other campus initiatives.

Marketing plans/strategies

Develops, creates, writes, implements, and/or evaluates individualized marketing plans and/or strategies for cultivation and solicitation of individual major gifts, gift planning, or corporate/foundation prospects (strategies typically require a high degree of innovation).
Attend meetings where strategies for principal gift-level prospects as well as prospects directly managed by the campaign director are discussed and help ensure that these strategies are developed in the context of the overall campaign strategy.

Executive advisor

Serves as an executive advisor for this area of expertise, interacting with prospects, donors, staff and outside professionals to provide information, advice and counsel regarding specialized program(s).
In partnership with AVC, Constituent Relations and AVC, Development, develop an internal communications strategy to keep colleagues within development/advancement and across the university apprised of campaign priorities, progress, and status.
Attend meetings of UDAR fundraising teams, including PGSI, Major Gifts, and SED, on a regular basis to facilitate coordination with prospects and campaign strategies.
Attend and participate as appropriate in key meetings related to the campaign, such as: Board of Trustees and select committee meetings, as appropriate.
Needs assessment and priority setting meetings.
Campaign volunteer leadership meetings, including unit based advisory groups. Meetings with key stakeholders to plan and implement multidisciplinary themes. Act as campaign liaison to other university offices as appropriate.
Convene specialized communities of practice to promote campaign goals and assessment

Prospect and volunteer constituencies

Creates, establishes and evaluates methods for building/maintaining prospect and volunteer constituencies and identifies, recruits, and directs the activities of high-level volunteers.
Working closely with the Vice Chancellor, provide staffing for the campaign chair/co-chairs and National Campaign Steering Committee, including: scheduling meetings; preparing agendas; briefing the Chancellor, Vice Chancellor, and campaign co-chairs; ensuring timely follow-up; and communicating committee decisions to relevant parties within development/advancement and across the university.
Develop individual relationships with NCSC co-chairs and members.
Oversee the development of campaign volunteer resources, such as handbooks, newsletters, and ongoing training opportunities to keep volunteers engaged with the campaign and its priorities, as well as high-level volunteer meetings and events, including the annual Volunteer Summit.

Fundraising and advancement programs / Fundraising goals

Analyzes needs and creates strategic and long-range plans for fundraising and other advancement programs and may have the authority to make commitments and precedent-setting decisions regarding program design, development, and procedures.
Working closely with appropriate colleagues in development/advancement services, including the AVC, Constituent Relations, AVC, PGSI, and AVC, Advancement, develop campaign gift tables, campaign counting and gift tagging protocols, campaign reports, and other tools required to track and report campaign progress, both for campus overall and individual units.
Ensures that predetermined fundraising goals are met.

Campaign team leadership

Manage and provide leadership for the campaign team. Establish and assess overall team strategy and goals. Mentor & coach team members.

Required Qualifications

Expert collaboration, relationship building, and trust building skills to work effectively with a broad range of stakeholders and partners.
Strong ability to navigate organizational complexities and decentralized environments and to lead successfully through influence.
Expert knowledge of comprehensive campaigns, particularly in a university setting.
Expert knowledge of various aspects of and functions in fundraising, such as donor and public relations, communications & marketing, planned giving, stewardship, and/or front-line fundraising, etc.
Expert knowledge of diverse stakeholder groups, teams, departments, achievements, and activities of a major and complex organization, including current issues of concern for both a research university campus and throughout higher education generally.
Expert knowledge of, and/or ability to quickly learn, the UC Berkeley campus including its vision, mission, goals, objectives, achievements and infrastructure; and/or demonstrated success in and expertise of (an) organization(s) with similarities to UC Berkeley.
Expert knowledge of all applicable laws, rules, regulations, risks, etc. in the nonprofit & fundraising field.
Expert written, oral, listening and interpersonal communication skills, including advanced political acumen, to establish and maintain good working relationships at all organizational levels and with outside constituencies, including donors and volunteers.
Expert skill in making persuasive and compelling presentations of campus goals/objectives and in securing gifts.
Expert analytical, critical thinking, problem solving, and conflict resolution skills.
Expert project/program management skills, including skill in setting and meeting program/project goals and objectives within budget and time constraints.
Demonstrated leadership experience, including the ability to build trust, influence others, and drive results.
Strong skills to lead and develop high-performing team(s), including setting strategic direction, establishing clear expectations, coaching staff, fostering collaboration, and managing accountability.

Education / Training

Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training. (Required)

This is a full-time (40 hours/week) career position eligible for UC benefits.

To apply, please submit your resume and cover letter.

About Verrado

Verrado is a large-scale master-planned community located in Buckeye, Arizona, in the foothills of the White Tank Mountains, 25 miles west of downtown Phoenix. Developed by Scottsdale-based developer DMB Associates, Inc., the community spans 8,800 acres and could include up to 14,080 homes and 4 million square feet of office, light industrial, and retail space.

Verrado's name is derived from the Spanish word “verdad,” which means truth and authenticity. Inspired by a vision of the future and timeless principles of town building, Verrado promises a remarkable way of life in the welcoming spirit of a great American small town. Homes throughout Verrado are designed to reflect the authentic architecture of the Southwest, while the community's small-town character creates a distinct sense of place.

Construction of the community began in the summer of 2002, and the first residents moved into Verrado in the summer of 2004.

Verrado is a place where possibilities abound to live life to the fullest. The streets themselves are amenities, leading to neighborhood parks, hiking trails, and two championship golf courses. The Center on Main, Heritage Swim Park, and community parks provide gathering places for activities and community events. Verrado also includes more than 21 miles of paths and trails running throughout the community and alongside its washes and mountain foothills.

Verrado is governed by three distinct, yet complementary nonprofit entities responsible for maintaining the vision and integrity of the community: Verrado Assembly, Inc., Verrado Community Association, Inc., and Victory District Association, Inc.
